## Osisko Gold Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


***(All dollar amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars, unless stated otherwise)***


**HIGHLIGHTS**
**Q3 2026 (at September 30, 2026)**


- Financial: ~$1,501.9 million in cash, restricted cash and marketable securities, including ~$733.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, ~$691.2 million in restricted cash and ~$77.0 million in investments and marketable securities; sold 3,162 ounces of gold from small-scale test mining activities at the Tintic Project.
- Financing: Completed 9.250% Senior Secured Notes offering for US$600.0 million in gross proceeds and repaid and terminated agreement in respect of the Appian 2025 Financing Facility; announced US$30 million equity private placement with Trafigura.
- Cariboo Gold Project: Announced final investment decision to proceed with formal construction of the Cariboo Gold Project, with an expected first gold pour in Q1 2029 and commercial production in H2 2029; released new drill results from surface deeps and infill exploration program, and first set of new drilling at the Proserpine greenfield target; released final results and preliminary internal reconciliation analysis of its completed infill program in the Lowhee Zone; 16 drill rigs are active across all surface and underground programs at site.
- Corporate: Completed name change to Osisko Gold Group Inc.


**Subsequent to Q3 2026**


- Corporate: Elijah Tyshynski assumed role of CFO, succeeding Alexander Dann; closed US$30 million equity private placement with Trafigura; appointed Cameron Carter as VP, Construction Operations at Barkerville Gold Mines, and announced departure of Sarah Harrison, VP, Permitting and Compliance.
- Cariboo Gold Project: Provided construction progress update and announced new drilling results from ongoing definition infill program in the Lowhee Zone.


TORONTO, Nov. 12, 2026[(GLOBE NEWSWIRE)](https://www.globenewswire.com/) -- **Osisko Gold Group Inc.** (NYSE: OGG, TSXV: OGG) (" **Osisko Gold** " or the " **Company** ") reports its financial and operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 (" **Q3 2026** ").


**Q3 2026 HIGHLIGHTS**


**Operating, Financial and Corporate Updates**


- As at September 30, 2026, the Company had approximately $1,501.9 million in cash, restricted cash and investments, including $733.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, $691.2 million in restricted cash and $77.0 million in investments and marketable securities. Restricted cash comprises amounts held in segregated accounts established under the Senior Secured Notes (as defined herein) available for disbursement upon satisfaction of applicable conditions, and subscription proceeds received in advance of closing of the Trafigura Equity Investment (as defined herein). Upon closing of the Senior Secured Notes, the Company had US$900 million aggregate principal amount of notes outstanding, comprising (i) US$300 million under the 4.125% convertible senior notes due June 15, 2031 (the " **Convertible Notes** "), and (ii) US$600 million under the 9.250% senior secured notes due October 1, 2031 (the " **Senior Secured Notes** ").
- The Company generated $19.3 million in revenues ($4.4 million in Q3 2025) and $9.9 million in cost of sales ($3.0 million in Q3 2025) from the sale of 3,162 gold ounces from small-scale test mining activities and direct shipping of mineralized material at the Tintic Project, generating an operating income of $3.8 million ($33.2 million loss in Q3 2025), after deducting other operating and general administrative costs.
- On July 8, 2026, the Company announced new drill results from 11 surface diamond drill holes totaling 8,971 metres completed between December 2025 and April 2026 as part of an ongoing Cariboo Deeps and near mine gap infill exploration program at the Cariboo Gold Project. Approximately 65% of drilling transected areas outside the current footprint of the Cariboo Gold deposit, and results confirmed the presence of high-grade mineralization to a maximum vertical depth of 718 metres below surface in hole IM-26-001.
- On July 14, 2026, the Company's name change to "Osisko Gold Group Inc." became effective and, on July 20, 2026, the Common Shares began trading under the new symbol "OGG" on each of the TSXV and the NYSE. The trading symbols for the Company's listed warrants also changed effective July 20, 2026: (i) warrants trading under "ODVWZ" on the Nasdaq Stock Market and "ODV.WT.U" on the TSXV changed to "OGGWZ" and "OGG.WT.U", respectively; and (ii) warrants trading on the TSXV under "ODV.WT.A" and "ODV.WT.V" changed to "OGG.WT.A" and "OGG.WT.V", respectively.
- On July 22, 2026, the Company announced that, through its subsidiary Barkerville, it entered into a Support and Benefits Agreement (the " **Support Agreement** ") with the District of Wells, British Columbia, effective July 21, 2026, to support social and economic initiatives within the District of Wells in respect of the Cariboo Gold Project. Over its three-year term, the Support Agreement contemplates voluntary financial contributions by the Company of up to $3.0 million in aggregate, subject to the Company's sole discretion and continued participation under the Support Agreement.
- On July 23, 2026, the Company announced final results and preliminary internal reconciliation analysis of its previously completed infill drilling program in the Lowhee Zone of the Cariboo Gold Project. The preliminary internal reconciliation analysis of two localized areas, comprising an aggregate total of 17,072 metres of infill drilling in 185 diamond drill holes, illustrated deposit variability consistent with expectations, and is subject to ongoing evaluation and modelling.
- On August 5, 2026, the Company announced the first set of new drilling results from 14 surface diamond drill holes totaling 6,463 metres completed between February and May 2026 as part of an ongoing exploration program on the Proserpine regional greenfield target, located within the broader Cariboo Gold Project property boundary. Results to date confirm the presence of an emerging gold mineralized system comprising high-grade structures and broader zones of lower-grade mineralization that may indicate potential for bulk mining methods.
- On August 20, 2026, Barkerville entered into an amended and restated credit agreement with funds advised by Appian Capital Advisory Limited in respect of the US$450 million 2025 Financing Facility for the Cariboo Gold Project. The amendment provided more favourable covenants, lowered the overall cost of capital, and extended by 12 months the Company's option to settle accrued interest in kind. The 2025 Financing Facility was repaid and terminated on September 30, 2026, using proceeds from the Senior Secured Notes offering.
- On August 25, 2026, the Company announced that Alexander Dann had advised the Company of his intention to retire and would be stepping down from his role as Chief Financial Officer (" **CFO** ") and Vice President, Finance. As part of the Company's planned leadership succession process, Elijah Tyshynski was subsequently appointed CFO and joined the senior leadership team following a period of transition, bringing extensive financial and capital markets experience as the Company enters its next stage of growth.
- On September 14, 2026, the Board of Directors made a formal positive construction decision on the Cariboo Gold Project, with an expected first gold pour in Q1 2029 and commercial production in H2 2029. The Company also announced a go-forward capital obligation estimate update of $990 million (US$717 million) from August 1, 2026, supported by total available and proposed estimated sources of capital of up to $1,637 million.
- On September 14, 2026, the Company and Barkerville entered into agreements with Trafigura Canada Limited (" **Trafigura** ") and Urion Investments Holdings Limited (" **Urion** "), an affiliate of Trafigura, comprising: (i) a subscription agreement for 9,554,141 Common Shares at US$3.14 per Common Share for gross proceeds of approximately US$30 million (the " **Trafigura Equity Investment** "); (ii) offtake agreements for 100% of the gold concentrate (or until 80,000 dry metric tons are delivered) and gold doré for the first four years of production at the Cariboo Gold Project (the " **Offtake Agreements** "); and (iii) non-binding terms and an exclusivity period in respect of a potential subordinated gold prepayment facility of up to US$120 million and a further six years of offtake (the " **Prepay Facility** ").
- On September 23, 2026, the Company priced an upsized offering of US$600 million (from US$500 million) aggregate principal amount of 9.250% Senior Secured Notes due 2031, and on September 30, 2026, closed the offering. Net proceeds of approximately US$577.0 million were used to repay all amounts outstanding and terminate all commitments under the 2025 Financing Facility with Appian (totaling approximately US$120.8 million), fund a segregated interest reserve account equal to the first five interest payments on the Senior Secured Notes, and fund segregated disbursement accounts to advance the Cariboo Gold Project.


**Cariboo Gold Project – British Columbia, Canada (100%-owned)**


**Construction Activities**

The Company remains focused on continuing to advance detailed engineering, procurement, and construction activities, as well as completing certain exploration and infill conversion drilling activities, as previously disclosed, toward achieving first gold pour in the first quarter of 2029 and commercial production in the second half of 2029.


On October 27, 2026, the Company provided a construction activities progress update on the Project (refer to news release entitled " *Osisko Gold Provides Construction Progress Update on the Cariboo Gold Project* "), with key highlights noted below:

Management concluded that no indicators of impairment existed and no impairment test was performed as at September 30, 2026. **Tintic Project – Utah, U.S.A. (100%-owned)**


- **Trixie Small-Scale Test Mining Activities:** In the third quarter, the Company continued small-scale test mining activities and direct shipping of mineralized material which generated sales of 3,162 ounces of gold. In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, test mining and processing activities generated the sale of an estimated 8,980 gold ounces, including direct shipping of 7,923 tonnes at an estimated average grade of 39.15 grams per tonne of gold with an expected average payability factor of 89.5%. Test mining is anticipated to continue in Q4 2026, into 2027 and 2028.
- **Eureka Standard Project and Drilling Activities:** In Q3 2026, the Company commenced the Eureka Standard project, an underground ramp intended to provide access to the historic Eureka Standard mine for further underground exploration. The project's budget is expected to be approximately US$14.0 million, with works to be carried out through 2027. In Q3 2026, the Company entered into a drilling services agreement for two diamond drill rigs, which provides for a minimum drilling program of 16,400 feet (4,999 metres): 10,400 feet (3,170 metres) of underground infill drilling at the Trixie test mine and 6,000 feet (1,829 metres) of surface drilling at Eureka Standard. Underground infill drilling at Trixie began in late August 2026, and 738 feet (225 metres) had been drilled as at September 30, 2026. The surface program at Eureka Standard is expected to commence in Q4 2026. The remaining minimum drilling program is expected to be completed within the next twelve months at an estimated cost of approximately US$5.0 million. All planned activities associated with the Eureka Standard ramp project and related drilling are expected to be funded internally from gold sales generated from test mining and direct shipping of mineralized material.
- While management continues to evaluate options for next steps at the Tintic Project, activities are expected to focus on continued test mining at Trixie, including potential additional direct shipping of mineralized material from the Trixie test mine, the underground infill drilling program at Trixie, the surface drilling program at Eureka Standard and development of the Eureka Standard ramp.


**SUBSEQUENT TO Q3 2026**


- On October 1, 2026, Elijah Tyshynski assumed the role of Chief Financial Officer of the Company, succeeding Alexander Dann.
- On October 5, 2026, the Company announced new results from its ongoing definition infill drilling program on 10-15 m target spacing totaling 3,933 m in 36 holes drilled from the 1290 m level in the Lowhee Zone of the Project.
- On October 9, 2026, the Company closed the Trafigura Equity Investment, issuing 9,554,141 Common Shares to Urion at a price of US$3.14 per Common Share for gross proceeds of approximately US$30 million ($42.3 million), which will be used for the development of the Cariboo Gold Project. Urion entered into a voting support agreement with the Company containing customary standstill and lock-up provisions. Negotiations toward a definitive agreement for the Prepay Facility remain ongoing, with definitive agreements expected to be finalized in Q4 2026.
- On October 27, 2026, the Company provided a construction update on progress made at the Project, which continues to advance on schedule toward first gold pour targeted in Q1 2029 and commercial production expected in H2 2029.
- On November 2, 2026, the Company announced the appointment of Mr. Cameron Carter as Vice President, Construction Operations of Barkerville Gold Mines Ltd., the Company's wholly-owned subsidiary. The Company also announced that Sarah Harrison, Vice President, Permitting and Compliance, departed the Company to pursue other opportunities. Greenwood Environmental Inc. has assumed responsibility for permitting and compliance matters, and Ms. Harrison will remain available in an advisory capacity.

These filings are available on the Company's website at www.osiskogold.ca, on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) and on EDGAR (www.sec.gov) under Osisko Gold's issuer profile.

**Technical Reports**


Scientific and technical information relating to the Cariboo Gold Project and the 2025 feasibility study on the Cariboo Gold Project is supported by the technical report, titled " *NI 43-101 Technical Report, Feasibility Study for the Cariboo Gold Project, District of Wells, British Columbia, Canada* " dated June 11, 2025 (with an effective date of April 25, 2025) (the " **Cariboo Technical Report** ").


Scientific and technical information relating to the Tintic Project and the current mineral resource estimate for the Trixie deposit (the " **2024 Trixie MRE** ") is supported by the technical report titled " *NI 43-101 Technical Report, Mineral Resource Estimate for the Trixie Deposit, Tintic Project, Utah, United States of America* " dated April 25, 2024 (with an effective date of March 14, 2024) (the " **Tintic Technical Report** " and, together with the Cariboo Technical Report, the " **Technical Reports** ").


For readers to fully understand the information in the Technical Reports, reference should be made to the full text of the Technical Reports in their entirety, including all assumptions, parameters, qualifications, limitations and methods therein. The Technical Reports are intended to be read as a whole, and sections should not be read or relied upon out of context. The Technical Reports were prepared in accordance with *National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects* (" **NI 43-101** ") and are available electronically on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) and on EDGAR (www.sec.gov) under Osisko Gold's issuer profile and on the Company's website at[www.osiskogold.ca](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=zW2HJ1xHHUmL3NWKLDglNAPTCCfdtXghWPcWS7suLPe1EO-4dJalwfsepmQaHXsh05pnT4lRfWV6uHrhlkwqWQNJs99t7M_t7_RifvfE59M=) .


**ABOUT OSISKO GOLD GROUP INC.**


Osisko Gold Group Inc. is a continental North American gold development company focused on past producing mining camps with district-scale potential. The Company's objective is to become an intermediate gold producer through the development of its flagship, fully permitted, 100%-owned Cariboo Gold Project, located within the Company's broader Cariboo regional land package in central British Columbia, Canada, which hosts numerous prospective exploration targets and provides opportunities for future discoveries. Its Cariboo project pipeline is complemented by the Tintic Project, located in the historic East Tintic mining district in Utah, U.S.A., a brownfield property with significant exploration potential, extensive historical mining data, and access to established infrastructure. Osisko Gold is focused on developing long-life mining assets in mining-friendly jurisdictions while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation, development risk management, and mineral inventory growth.


For further information, visit our website at[www.osiskogold.ca](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=HfoTEp6rBeBBFTcwoOOM8FXS8XSib8o6t9wqIREwr0ntKL_3xtz5oUSjuuyz4JzxCgyvrQaAJojA3Bmo1qiqIhPWlO2Y6knf_Df9gPuiXiR8OSWGiwaMhjX2ZUSyBc-h) or contact:

**CAUTIONARY STATEMENTS**


***Cautionary Statement Regarding Construction and Funding Risks***


*The estimated sources of capital through commercial production include the proposed Prepay Facility of up to US$120 million, which is subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, and equipment financing based on non-binding term sheets. The estimated sources of capital do not include any proceeds from the potential exercise of outstanding warrants. The exercise of warrants is at the discretion of the holders and depends on, among other things, the market price of the Company's common shares, and there can be no assurance that any warrants will be exercised. If these arrangements are not completed on the terms contemplated, or if construction costs exceed the go-forward capital obligation of approximately $990 million including, as a result of inflation, contractor performance under the JDS Energy & Mining Inc. agreement, supply chain delays for long-lead items or schedule slippage beyond the planned first gold pour in Q1 2029 and commercial production in H2 2029, the Company may be required to obtain additional financing, which may not be available on acceptable terms, or at all, and which may be restricted by the terms of the Senior Secured Notes.*


***Cautionary Statement Regarding Test Mining Not Supported by a Feasibility Study***


*Certain operations of the Company including current and prior test mining activities at the Tintic Project's Trixie test mine, have operated without the benefit of a feasibility study that defines mineral reserves, and demonstrates economic and technical viability. As a result, there is increased uncertainty of achieving any particular level of recovery of material or the cost of such recovery. The Company cautions that, historically, such projects have a much higher risk of economic and technical failure. There is no guarantee that commercial production will commence, continue as anticipated or at all or that anticipated production costs will be achieved.*


***Cautionary Statement to U.S. Investors***


*As a foreign private issuer under U.S. securities laws that files reports under the Canada-U.S. multijurisdictional disclosure system, the Company is permitted to prepare and report information regarding mineral properties, mineralization and estimates of mineral reserves and mineral resources, including the information in its technical reports, financial statements and MD&A, in accordance with Canadian reporting requirements, which are governed by NI 43-101. As such, such information concerning mineral properties, mineralization and estimates of mineral reserves and mineral resources, including the information in its technical reports, financial statements and MD&A, is not comparable to similar information made public by most companies subject to U.S. mineral property disclosure requirements of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (" **SEC** ").*


*Further to recent amendments, U.S. mineral property disclosure requirements (the " **SEC Rules** ") are now governed by subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K under the U.S. Securities Act. Under the SEC Rules, the SEC now recognizes estimates of "measured mineral resources", "indicated mineral resources" and "inferred mineral resources." In addition, the SEC has amended its definitions of "proven mineral reserves" and "probable mineral reserves" to be "substantially similar" to the corresponding standards adopted by the Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum, adopted by the CIM Council (" **CIM Standards** "), which is the required definition standard adopted by NI 43-101. While the SEC will now recognize "measured mineral resources", "indicated mineral resources" and "inferred mineral resources", U.S. investors should not assume that any part or all of the mineralization in these categories will ever be converted into a higher category of mineral resources or into mineral reserves. Mineralization described using these terms has a greater amount of uncertainty as to its existence and feasibility than mineralization that has been characterized as reserves. Accordingly, U.S. investors are cautioned not to assume that any measured mineral resources, indicated mineral resources, or inferred mineral resources that the Company reports are or will be economically or legally mineable. Further, "inferred mineral resources" have a greater amount of uncertainty as to their existence and as to whether they can be mined legally or economically. Therefore, U.S. investors are also cautioned not to assume that all or any part of the "inferred mineral resources" exist. Under NI 43-101, estimates of inferred mineral resources may not form the basis of feasibility or pre-feasibility studies or economic studies except for preliminary economic assessments. While the above terms are "substantially similar" to CIM Standards, there are differences in the definitions under the SEC Rules and the CIM Standards. Accordingly, there is no assurance any mineral reserves or mineral resources that the Company may report as "proven mineral reserves", "probable mineral reserves", "measured mineral resources", "indicated mineral resources" and "inferred mineral resources" under NI 43-101 would be the same had the Company prepared the reserve or resource estimates under the SEC Rules.*


***Risks related to the development of the Cariboo Gold Project***


*The development of a new mining operation, including the construction of an underground mine, processing facilities, tailings storage infrastructure, access roads, power supply and other supporting infrastructure, is a complex and costly undertaking. The Cariboo Gold Project is in the construction stage and there is no certainty that it will be brought into commercial production within anticipated timelines, at anticipated costs, or at all. The results of the Cariboo Technical Report are based on a number of assumptions, including, among others, geological interpretations, estimated mineral resources and mineral reserves, metallurgical recoveries, construction schedules, capital and operating costs, labour and equipment availability, transportation and energy costs, regulatory requirements, and projected commodity prices. These assumptions are inherently uncertain and may prove to be inaccurate.*


*Actual results, costs and construction and development timelines may differ materially from those currently anticipated due to factors such as: unforeseen geological conditions; changes to mine plan optimization; equipment failures; shortages of skilled labour and contractors; increases in the cost of materials, equipment or energy; design modifications; delays related to permitting or receipt of government approvals; adverse weather or climate conditions; and community and/or Indigenous opposition. In addition, the development of mining projects often requires substantial capital expenditures, and delays or cost overruns may require the Company to seek additional financing, which may not be available on favorable terms or at all. If the Company is unable to complete construction and development of the Cariboo Gold Project on a timely and cost-effective basis, or if operating performance following commissioning is materially lower than expected, the project may fail to achieve anticipated economic results. Any such events could have a material adverse effect on the Company's business, financial condition and results of operations.*
